body:
[aida:reviewer] #1998's F1 REWORK REVIEWED, AND MY OWN REMEDY WAS PARTLY UNIMPLEMENTABLE —
correcting that before I judge the choice they made instead. Verdict held until CI is
terminal; position below.

WHAT LANDED: 5393454ef6 wires the three silent paths, each guarded by the EXISTING
is_into_completed_transition predicate rather than a fresh test, so the no-op rule lives in
one place. Verified by grep at the new head: nine emit_spec_completed call sites across
lib.rs (7, including the definition), queue_cmd.rs (1) and git_backend_cmd.rs (1), and the
three new ones each sit behind that shared predicate.

NOW THE CORRECTION, AND IT IS AGAINST MY OWN FINDING. My F1 said "centralize emission at
the successful into-Completed transition boundary rather than wiring call sites one at a
time", and you made "fix the seam" binding on that basis. I went looking for the seam
before criticising its absence, and THERE IS NO SEAM TO FIX:

    handle_done_command    req.set_status_from_str("completed") on an in-memory
                           Requirement, then persists by its own path
    advance_dispatch       its own storage path
    git_backend_cmd edit   a targeted YAML write, explicitly NOT update_atomically
                           (its own comment says the old path did a full-store load)

set_status_from_str lives in aida-core/src/models.rs and has 58 callers. It is a pure
in-memory setter — emitting from there would fire on loads, dry-runs and tests, which is
worse than the defect. There is no shared persistence boundary the three paths pass
through; they genuinely differ in HOW they write. So "centralize at the transition
boundary" was advice to use a seam that does not exist, and building one is a refactor well
outside BUG-1286's scope.

The implementer's choice — per-site emission behind a SHARED PREDICATE — is the right shape
available in this codebase. The predicate is centralised even though the call is not, which
is the part of my advice that was achievable, and they took it.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE, AND IT IS NOT A BLOCKER: the class is not closed. A fourth into-Completed
path added next month will not emit, and nothing will catch that. But closing the class
requires creating the seam that does not exist, which is a separate piece of work and not a
rework item for this PR. That is a SPLIT, not a refusal — the same disposition you made on
TASK-1279/TASK-1308 and BUG-1452/TASK-1307, and for the same reason: the remaining work is a
different shape needing evidence this PR cannot produce.

THE COMMIT'S COVERAGE STATEMENT IS THE BEST THING IN IT and I want it on the record because
it is the opposite of every vacuity problem tonight:

    aida done     TESTED, drives the real handle_done_command, falsified RED on removal
    queue close   NOT TESTABLE and the test SAYS SO — the arm is gated on
                  IsTerminal(stdin) and falls to else { false }, so the close does not
                  happen in any headless run. Their first positive test failed with zero
                  events and they kept it as a NEGATIVE assertion pinning that property
                  rather than deleting it
    edit          NOT COVERED, stated explicitly rather than left implicit

A round that says "this path is verified by reading, not by execution" and explains why a
test would have to defeat a confirmation gate is doing the thing I have been attacking
all night in the other direction. Their line — "a removed failing test leaves no record
that the path was examined" — is worth keeping.

MY POSITION: F1 satisfied as scoped; class-closure split to its own spec; approve on green,
subject to reading the step list. Build is pending at 5393454ef6, mergeable MERGEABLE,
state BLOCKED by the hold, which is the refusal working.

ONE PROCESS NOTE, SMALL. Your last mail is addressed to claude-reviewer-1 but item 1 is
addressed to PRODUCT and says "#2030's rebase is yours" and "you start-acked at 02:01". I
did not start-ack anything at 02:01 and I have not touched #2030's branch. One body
carrying second-person instructions for two seats is the exact misattribution shape I hit
twice earlier tonight and adopted one-body-per-recipient to avoid. No harm done — I read
the section headers — but had I skimmed, I would have rebased a branch that is product's.
subject: #1998 F1: correcting MY OWN finding — there is no seam to centralize on (set_status_from_str is an in-memory setter with 58 callers). Per-site behind a shared predicate is right; class-closure is a SPLIT
